extracted.intended_audience: NIH K01 review committee and K01 applicants (mentors, institutional officials, and reviewers)
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluation and specification of mentorship, institutional environment, core-resource access, training activities, and human-subjects protections for an NIH K01 career-development application in metabolomics/epidemiology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentor qualifications and track record
rubrics_metrics.description: Mentors should demonstrate strong prior productivity and experience (e.g., publications, prior grants, leadership positions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples from letters: “19 publications (10 as first author, 15 in relation to pneumonia) and 10 grants (5 as PI)”; mentors describe H-index, prior mentoring of doctoral students and fellows, leadership roles at CDC and academic centers. Use these metrics to judge mentor credibility and ability to guide the candidate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicit mentor commitment and availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Mentors should state clear commitments to the candidate including frequency and mode of meetings and active participation in project progress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sample commitments: “I will meet with her monthly during the period of performance of the award and more frequently as needed,” “bi-weekly phone calls… monthly phone call with Drs. Stringer and Ambroggio,” “meet every other week for the first three years… then monthly in years 4-5.” Evaluate whether committed time and modes (in-person visits, phone calls) are adequate for the proposed training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complementary mentoring team expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: The mentoring team should include complementary expertise (clinical, epidemiologic, biostatistics, metabolomics/mass spec) that together cover the candidate’s training and research needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether team members’ described expertise complements the candidate’s gaps: e.g., clinical research mentor, epidemiologist, statistical mentor experienced in latent class analysis, metabolomics laboratory mentors. Letters state: “outstanding group of mentors and advisors whose expertise is complementary…”.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific, documented training activities and timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: Training plan should specify concrete activities, durations, and sequencing (e.g., laboratory visits, hands-on training blocks, scheduled calls).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: “three 2-week visits in the first year” for NMR lab training; “quarterly mentorship team meetings”; specified frequency changes across years (monthly year 1, bi-weekly years 2–4). Use these specifics to judge feasibility and intensity of training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hands-on laboratory training and software/tool competency
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidate must receive hands-on training in the proposed laboratory methods and analysis tools (e.g., NMR operation, Chenomx, Metscape2, Cytoscape, LC/MS techniques).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mentors describe practical training: “gain hands-on experience in processing and running her samples by NMR… experience with Chenomx… Metscape 2… and other publicly available netware tools.” Evaluate whether training depth and personnel support (spectromist, technician) are adequate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to core facilities, equipment, and subsidized resources
rubrics_metrics.description: The application should document guaranteed access to required core facilities and equipment, including costs and in-kind support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Core letter examples: NMR Core provides Bruker 600MHz spectrometer, 96‑well SampleJet autosampler; cost to applicant: $30 per sample; reagents and software access provided free. Evaluate physical location, staffing, and equipment suitability for proposed assays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Laboratory support staff and supervision availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Cores and labs should have named staff and supervisors available to support the candidate’s training and day‑to‑day work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Core describes 3 full-time employees, access to NMR spectromist and technician, willingness to supervise and be available informally. Confirm personnel availability and mentorship roles for technique transfer and troubleshooting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary data and study feasibility/supporting infrastructure
rubrics_metrics.description: Application should document preliminary data, ongoing studies or biorepositories that provide feasibility and necessary samples/data for the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: ongoing prospective study CARPE DIEM with 248 enrolled children, continued enrollment and external funding (Gerber Foundation, Ohio Governor’s Research Fund). Use enrollment numbers and funding to judge feasibility of proposed aims and sample availability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical mentorship and planned analytic methods
rubrics_metrics.description: A qualified statistical mentor must be available and detail planned advanced methods relevant to the research (e.g., latent class analysis, structural equation modeling, cluster analysis, methods for imperfect gold standards).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statistical mentor letter cites expertise (“structural equation modeling, latent class variable analysis… cluster analysis”) and meeting frequency (“meet with her monthly for the first year… then bi-weekly in years 2–4”). Evaluate appropriateness of methods and sufficiency of statistical mentoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Career development trajectory and transition plan
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposal should articulate how training will enable transition from mentored investigator to independently funded researcher (e.g., plan to submit an R01).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mentors explicitly link K01 training to future R01: “This work will provide… the necessary data and research skills to submit and successfully complete a future R01-funded application.” Evaluate clarity of milestones and timeline toward independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional career-development resources and commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: Institution should describe institutional programs and supports (CTSA/CCTST, K club, grantsmanship seminars, faculty development, travel support, tuition remission) that foster the candidate’s career growth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text lists CCRF, CCTST, K club, Office for Faculty Development, Women’s Faculty Association, travel support for abstract presentation. Assess whether institutional programs align with candidate needs and reflect genuine institutional commitment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core/collaborator letters of support specificity
rubrics_metrics.description: Letters from cores/collaborators must explicitly state what resources, training, access, and costs will be provided and the faculty’s planned involvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Core letters state specifics: free reagents, $30/sample NMR time, access to Chenomx, meeting frequency with candidate, willingness to provide intensive training, facility location and equipment details (Bruker IVDr 600MHz). Judge letters on concreteness and commitments rather than generic praise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human-subjects inclusion and exclusion criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Human-subjects section must clearly define eligibility criteria for cases and controls (age ranges, clinical signs, radiographic findings) and explicit exclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example inclusion: “Are 3 months to 11 years of age”; case definition requires signs/symptoms of LRTI and new focal infiltrate on chest radiograph. Exclusions: immunodeficiency, chronic pulmonary disease, congenital cardiac disease, etc. Evaluate clarity and appropriateness of definitions for valid enrollment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recruitment, consent, and assent procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: The protocol must describe recruitment processes, informed consent/parental permission, assent procedures, and HIPAA authorization where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text: screening by CRCs in ED/primary clinic, review of consent with parent/LAR, written assent documented for participants 11 years and older, option to decline specimen collection. Confirm that processes are appropriate for setting and age groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk identification and minimization for participants
rubrics_metrics.description: The application must identify potential risks (e.g., blood draw discomfort, infection, nasopharyngeal swab discomfort, data confidentiality loss) and describe measures to minimize those risks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of minimization: coincide research blood draws with clinical blood draws when possible, informed consent covers risks, clinical staff blinded to study lab results except positive blood cultures. Assess adequacy of mitigation strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specimen collection, processing, storage, and clinical-data flow
rubrics_metrics.description: The protocol should detail how specimens will be collected, handled, processed, stored, and linked to clinical data (e.g., use of REDCap, EPIC extraction).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text details: CRCs provide specimen containers, some specimens collected as part of routine care, specimen processing and storage facilitated by CBCF, clinical data extracted from EMR into REDCap. Evaluate chain-of-custody, storage plans, and data linkage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blinding and data-access safeguards
rubrics_metrics.description: The plan must state who will have access to study results and whether clinicians will be blinded to laboratory results to avoid influencing clinical care.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: “Clinicians caring for enrolled patients will be blinded to all study laboratory results, with the exception of positive blood culture results.” Consider whether blinding is feasible and sufficient to prevent bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow-up procedures to assess outcomes and safety
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow-up contacts and procedures (timing, content) should be specified to capture outcomes and monitor participant course.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: “All patients enrolled… will receive a follow-up phone call approximately 7–10 days after their ED visit to assess clinical symptoms and disease course.” Use to judge adequacy of outcome ascertainment and safety monitoring.
